title: Acids and Bases
text: Acids are substances that donate hydrogen ions (protons) in solution and taste sour, such as vinegar (acetic acid) and citrus fruit (citric acid). Bases accept hydrogen ions or donate hydroxide ions and taste bitter, such as baking soda and soap. When an acid and a base react, they neutralize each other to form water and a salt. Strong acids and bases fully ionize in water, while weak ones only partially ionize.
